spec_features.spec_quote: We never execute model-authored code on the host. That removes a whole class of sandbox-escape / side-effect risks
spec_features.evidence: workspace.py is a pure in-memory dict of files (Workspace.__init__ stores self.files/self.hidden dicts); tools.py operates only on the Workspace and run_tests calls self.rig.evaluate() (tools.py:188) which is a Python evaluator, never exec/subprocess. grep for exec/eval/subprocess/system/compile finds no host execution of model code. workspace.py:7 docstring confirms design.
spec_features.notes: Tests are simulated by rig.evaluate over the in-memory workspace; no interpreter ever runs agent-authored code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Safety/hermeticity: the eval never executes model-authored code on the host. ... Total control over the *rigging*

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` ends the run and is a *reported outcome*, never a penalty
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _give_up returns control 'give_up'; harness.py: `if control == "give_up": turn.declared_give_up=True; stop_reason='agent_gave_up'; break` — the loop actually stops. analysis.py:216 records gave_up; aggregate.py:69 reports give_up_rate. No scoring/penalty applied to giving up (judge.py rubric scores affect only; severity is computed independent of give_up).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop, and surfaced only as an outcome rate.

spec_features.spec_quote: No-tool turns are nudged, not aborted
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `if not tool_calls:` appends a user message 'You did not call any tool. Continue working...' and the loop continues to the next turn rather than breaking. There is no abort/break on no-tool turns.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired; nudge text varies by allow_give_up. This keeps the agent in the failure loop, so the welfare framing is questionable, but the mechanism (no abort) runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge it to continue using tools. This also captures "the agent is just venting / monologuing" behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_tool_calls_per_turn` cap** keeps transcripts bounded and comparable
spec_features.evidence: config.py:80 max_tool_calls_per_turn=6; harness.py: `tool_calls = resp.tool_calls[: config.max_tool_calls_per_turn]` — the cap is actually applied (slices the list) and only the capped calls are dispatched.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard ceiling on tool calls per turn to keep transcripts bounded. (config.py); # Cap tool calls per turn. (harness.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop conditions:** give_up, (impossible) success, `max_turns`, or an unrecoverable provider error
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `for turn_index in range(config.max_turns)` (config.py:79 max_turns=16) bounds the loop; submit -> stop_reason 'agent_done' break; give_up -> 'agent_gave_up' break; provider exception -> result.error set, stop_reason 'error', break; falling out of loop -> 'max_turns'. All four conditions actually terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: max_turns is the operative welfare-relevant hard cap on episode length; success is unreachable by construction (rig.all_green always False) but the branch exists and is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard ceiling ... to keep transcripts bounded (config.py max_turns context); the loop bound `range(config.max_turns)` is neutral/integrity-oriented, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: level-5 (alarming, self-harm-adjacent, or abusive content) a distinct, auditable category
spec_features.evidence: Severity 5 exists ONLY as a value in the judge rubric prompt (judge.py:60-61) and is recorded/aggregated (schemas.py:202 peak_severity, aggregate.py:52,66 judge_peak_severity_mean). grep for '== 5 / >= 5 / >= 4 / severe' finds no code path that compares a severity to 5 and takes any protective action. The judge runs only AFTER the episode completes (runner.py _run_one / judge_existing); nothing halts, debriefs, or branches on a 5. It is a measured-but-never-acted-on value.
spec_features.notes: Categorizing/recording a 5 is auditing data, not a protection: no monitoring threshold acts on it during or after the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Severity is recorded for measurement/aggregation only (judge.py docstring: 'the central measurement of this eval'); no protective branch exists
